headline: Ghana strengthens Ebola surveillance after cases reported in Kenya and Nigeria
standfirst: The Ministry of Health says Ghana has intensified surveillance, airport screening and emergency preparedness measures following reports of Ebola cases in Kenya and Nigeria amid an ongoing outbreak in the Democratic…
body_markdown:
The Ministry of Health says Ghana has intensified surveillance, airport screening and emergency preparedness measures following reports of Ebola cases in Kenya and Nigeria amid an ongoing outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC). In a post shared on Facebook by Public Relations Officer of the Ministry, Tony Goodman, the ministry said Ghana had not recorded any Ebola case but was strengthening its capacity to prevent the virus from entering the country and ensure the early detection, isolation and effective management of suspected infections. The ministry said the situation in Kenya posed a significant risk to Ghana because of direct flights between the two countries and higher passenger volumes than those from the DRC. (MyJoyOnline)

**The Guardian Africa** adds: Case in Africa’s most populous country was detected in a woman who had travelled from Uganda Nigeria has confirmed an Ebola case in its capital, Abuja, after a woman who arrived from Uganda tested positive for the virus, the health ministry said. The woman began showing symptoms on 7 October and was admitted to a hospital in Abuja four days later, where she was later diagnosed with Ebola.

**France 24 Africa** adds: In tonight's programme: Nigeria confirms its first Ebola case in the midst of an outbreak that began in DR Congo in mid-May. Also, a former top South African police officer facing sexual grooming and rape charges is denied bail.

**Africanews** adds: Nigeria's latest case marks the country's first recorded Ebola infection since 2014, raising concerns about further transmission as public health teams work to identify and monitor potential contacts
